title: Computer Secure Channel and Netlogon Trust Health
summary: Understand how a domain member maintains its machine-account trust with Active Directory and how to distinguish DNS, DC-location, credential and secure-channel failures.
objective: Explain what the secure channel protects, identify the evidence that proves a trust failure, and select the correct diagnostic tool for a member computer versus a domain controller.
body_outline: Domain-joined computers maintain a machine-account relationship with the domain and use Netlogon-backed secure-channel operations for trust verification.
Test-ComputerSecureChannel is appropriate for domain member computers and returns a Boolean health result; Microsoft explicitly cautions that it can report false positives on domain controllers.
For domain controllers, use domain-controller-appropriate tools such as netdom or nltest rather than treating the member-computer cmdlet as authoritative.
A broken secure-channel symptom can overlap with DNS, time, Kerberos and DC-locator problems, so collect those dependencies before repairing the trust.
quick_check: Why should Test-ComputerSecureChannel not be used as the sole trust-health test on a domain controller?

title: Domain Member Trust Failure: Evidence Before Repair
summary: Use a bounded diagnostic sequence for the classic trust-relationship failure without immediately resetting machine credentials or rejoining the domain.
symptoms: The trust relationship between this workstation and the primary domain failed
Domain logon fails after a machine rollback or stale snapshot
A member server intermittently loses domain authentication
diagnostic_order: Confirm the system is a domain member rather than a domain controller.
Verify DNS client configuration and DC discovery before declaring the machine trust broken.
Check time source and clock offset because Kerberos/time failures can mimic broader authentication faults.
Run Test-ComputerSecureChannel with verbose output on the member computer and capture the result.
Only if the secure channel is proven broken should an approved repair/reset be planned using a supported method and suitable credentials.
escalation_boundary: This runbook is read-only. Do not use -Repair, netdom reset, unjoin/rejoin, machine-account deletion or password reset until the failure is evidenced and change authority is confirmed.

title: Replication Operations: From Repadmin Evidence to Root Cause
summary: Turn replication status into an operational decision by correlating Repadmin, Directory Service events, site topology, DNS and authentication evidence.
objective: Classify a replication failure by evidence rather than by error code alone and identify when the issue belongs to topology, DNS, authentication, transport, database health or an intentionally offline DC.
body_outline: Replication failures can originate in topology, WAN connectivity, DNS, authentication/authorization, directory-database processing or intentionally offline domain controllers.
Repadmin and Directory Service event logs provide complementary evidence; neither should be interpreted without topology and timing context.
A staging DC or long-offline DC can legitimately accumulate replication age, but once age approaches or exceeds tombstone lifetime the operational response changes materially.
Daily replication-health monitoring and timely fault resolution reduce the chance that a localized issue becomes a directory-consistency or recovery problem.
quick_check: Why is a single Repadmin error code insufficient to decide whether a domain controller should be rebuilt?

title: Replication Failure Triage: Topology, DNS, Authentication or Database
summary: Apply a repeatable evidence-first decision tree before forcing replication, removing a DC or changing topology.
symptoms: Directory Service events identify a partner or transport error
one site is stale while others converge normally
replication age is approaching tombstone-lifetime risk
diagnostic_order: Record the exact failing source, destination, naming context, error and first/last failure timestamps.
Check whether the DC is intentionally offline, staged or isolated.
Validate DNS resolution, DC Locator and network reachability between the affected partners.
Correlate Directory Service events and authentication errors before changing topology.
Check site/subnet/link design against the real WAN topology.
If the failure cannot be corrected safely and the DC is no longer recoverable, follow supported decommission/forced-removal and metadata-cleanup procedures rather than improvising.
escalation_boundary: Do not force metadata cleanup, seize FSMO roles, disable security controls or repeatedly force synchronization simply to clear an error. Escalate when replication age, compromise, database damage or unrecoverable DC state changes the recovery boundary.

title: Active Directory Senior Operations Final Checkpoint
summary: Final scenario assessment spanning secure channels, replication triage, recovery-point trust, time hierarchy and lifecycle decisions.

assessment_items.question: A member server reports a broken trust after a VM rollback. What must be proven before repairing its secure channel?
assessment_items.answer: Confirm member-computer role, DNS/DC discovery, time health and an actual failed secure-channel test; then use an approved repair method rather than immediately deleting or rejoining the machine account.

assessment_items.question: A DC has replication errors but was intentionally offline for staging. What additional variable changes the risk decision?
assessment_items.answer: Replication age relative to tombstone lifetime and whether the DC can safely re-enter the topology without carrying stale directory data.

assessment_items.question: Why might the newest domain-controller backup be rejected during a security incident?
assessment_items.answer: It may have been taken after compromise or corruption; recovery should use the latest trusted recovery point, not automatically the newest backup.

assessment_items.question: Why should time-source evidence be captured during Kerberos or trust troubleshooting?
assessment_items.answer: AD authentication depends on acceptable time consistency, so clock-source or offset faults can present as authentication/trust symptoms.

title: Principal-Level AD Operations and Recovery Interview
summary: Evidence-driven architecture and incident questions covering replication, secure-channel faults, trusted recovery points, lifecycle and recovery governance.

questions.question: You inherit a forest with intermittent replication, stale DCs and no tested recovery drill. What is your first-week operating model?
answer_points: identify stale or intentionally offline DCs
do not perform broad cleanup until evidence classifies each failure

questions.question: How do you distinguish a member-computer trust failure from a domain-controller secure-channel problem?
answer_points: use Test-ComputerSecureChannel only for member computers
use netdom or nltest for DC secure-channel validation

questions.question: What makes an AD recovery plan operational rather than merely documented?
answer_points: post-recovery validation and lessons incorporated into the plan
